status_summary: On 2025-03-26 DOL cancelled ILAB grants and contracts, including Better Work and worker safety projects, as reported by Fashion Dive the next day, which cites a government efficiency office post and no DOL statement. From 2025-06-04 the United States filed a series of USMCA rapid response requests on alleged denial of organizing rights at Mexican facilities, and on 2025-08-19 DOL announced an updated DHS-led forced labor enforcement strategy in which ILAB co-chairs the Entity List subcommittee. On 2026-01-12 ILAB awarded about 23 million dollars for Mexican labor law enforcement and on 2026-04-08 coordinated the launch of voluntary supply chain tools, with releases describing ILAB's mission as combating foreign labor abuse and unfair trade practices to support U.S. job and wage growth. No formal reorganization or published refocusing directive was found.

timeline.event: DOL cancels ILAB grants and contracts, including Better Work and worker safety projects (reported by Fashion Dive on 2025-03-27; no DOL statement located).

United States seeks review under the USMCA rapid response labor mechanism of alleged interference with union supporters at an automobile wheel plant in Chihuahua, Mexico (Release 25-932-NAT, the 36th request), the first of eight such requests on the ILAB release listing through 2026-06-12.

DOL announces the updated 2025 Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act enforcement strategy of the DHS-led Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force, adding five priority sectors; ILAB co-chairs the Entity List subcommittee (Release 25-1218-NAT).
ILAB awards more than 23 million dollars to strengthen labor law enforcement in Mexico under the USMCA, framed around American jobs and wage growth (Release No. 25-1605-NAT).

United States reports a second win before a USMCA panel in a labor rights dispute at a Mexican critical minerals mine (title and date from the ILAB release listing; the individual release was not opened).

DOL, with ILAB coordinating, launches four voluntary supply chain tools (LaborShield, ImportWatch, SourcingStrong and a traceability portal) aimed at foreign labor abuse and unfair trade practices (Release 26-591-NAT).

United States seeks Mexico's review of alleged denial of workers' rights at a mining facility under the USMCA rapid response mechanism (title and date from the ILAB release listing; the individual release was not opened).

title: Refocus ILAB on foreign labor violations that harm U.S. workers and on trade enforcement
uncertainties: The grant and contract cancellations rest on trade press (Fashion Dive, 2025-03-27), which reports a government efficiency office post and trade association reaction and includes no DOL statement; no DOL release on the cancellations was found. The releases of 2025-06-04, 2025-08-19 and 2026-04-08 and the ILAB release listing were read on dol.gov on 2026-10-18; the 2026-01-12 release was read in an earlier review and by the researcher. The 2026-03-27 and 2026-06-12 events are known from titles and dates on the ILAB listing only. The Federal Register API returned no ILAB rules. The 2025-08-19 strategy is a DHS-led interagency product, so ILAB's part is a contribution to it. Whether the changes are a refocusing or simply a contraction is an interpretation; the rapid response cases concern organizing rights and the China strategy concerns forced labor, two of the categories the text names. No directive confining ILAB to trade enforcement was located.
